independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently against verse_map_web.json: vv1-3 are direct second-person plea to Yahweh, and v4's causal clause (MT כִּי, 'For you are not a God...') supplies the ground for that plea rather than opening a new topic, so the block sustains one continuous address through v6's 'Yahweh abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful man' (third-person aside inside a second-person block, not an addressee change). The seam at 5.6|5.7 rests on the adversative independent-pronoun construction that opens the next row (collate-verified below), a textbook-strength discourse pivot, so the strophe correctly ends immediately before it. Superscription labels (mizmor, lamnatseach, le-David, el-hannechilot) collate exactly against psalm_device_inventory.json's Ps 5 entry, and web:Ps.5.0=oshb:Ps.5.1 is arithmetically correct (Ps 5 is a shift+1 psalm per web_mt_offset_map.json, independently re-derived). The rejected_alternative (a break after the morning plea, v3) is well-grounded: v4's causal connector argues against, not merely 'no seam signal.' No selah or K/Q instance falls in this span (checked against pmarks_Ps.json). Confidence 'high' is earned by the cleanliness of the 5.6|5.7 pivot.

The cited pivot וַאֲנִ֗י at web:Ps.5.7 (=oshb:Ps.5.8) collates at byte tier exactly as claimed (collate.py, verified against verse_map_oshb.json, not hand-typed). Internal-seam candidates were tested and found weaker than the writer's chosen boundary: MT 5.10 (=web 5.9, 'For there is no faithfulness...') opens with the explanatory particle כִּי, subordinating it to the preceding plea rather than opening independent material; MT 5.11 (=web 5.10, the imprecation) returns to direct imperative address to the same addressee (Elohim), not a new party; MT 5.12 (=web 5.11, the blessing) opens with a plain conjunctive-vav jussive (וְיִשְׂמְחוּ), a materially weaker discourse marker than the fronted independent pronoun that opens the strophe. So the rejected_alternative's 'no renewed address shift' holds up under closer grammatical inspection, not merely as an assertion. A K/Q note at MT 5.9 (=web 5.8, הושר/הַיְשַׁר) falls inside this span but is never Hebrew-quoted by the row, so no disclosure was owed (K/Q disclosure binds to quoted verses only) — check_marks.py confirms 0 flags. Confidence 'high' is appropriate given no rival internal seam in this span carries comparable weight to the opening pivot.

Superscription labels (mizmor, lamnatseach, le-David, al-hashsheminit) collate against the inventory (which additionally carries 'binginot' — the row doesn't claim it, which is not an omission error since rows aren't required to recite every label). web:Ps.6.0=oshb:Ps.6.1 and the shift+1 arithmetic for Ps 6 is independently confirmed via web_mt_offset_map.json (k=1). vv1-7 sustain uninterrupted second-person address to Yahweh (imperative plea through the weeping description); the seam against v8 rests on a genuine addressee shift (imperative to 'workers of iniquity', a new party never addressed in vv1-7) rather than mere topic drift — this is a textbook-clean tier-1 driver. The rejected break after v3's 'how long?' correctly notes no addressee change occurs there. A K/Q note at MT 6.4 (=web 6.3) falls in this span but is not Hebrew-quoted, so disclosure was not owed (check_marks.py: 0 flags). No selah in this span (confirmed against pmarks_Ps.json). Confidence 'high' is well-earned — this division is close to uncontested.

ס֣וּרוּ at web:Ps.6.8 (=oshb:Ps.6.9) collates at byte tier exactly as claimed (verified via collate.py against source bytes, not retyped). This is the mirror half of the addressee-shift seam already tested under M8-Ps-010: the plural imperative addressed to 'workers of iniquity' is a new party absent from the preceding lament, and the closing declaration of the enemies' coming shame (v10) continues that same third-person frame rather than reverting to petition. No rival seam candidate exists inside this three-verse span (v9's 'Yahweh has heard' repetition is anaphoric reinforcement of the same confidence movement, not a competing pivot). Confidence 'high' matches the strength of the addressee-shift driver.

Title labels (shiggaion, le-David) and the Cush-the-Benjamite historical note collate against the inventory and the WEB title text; web:Ps.7.0=oshb:Ps.7.1 and shift+1 arithmetic (independently confirmed, k=1) are correct. Selah placement is verified against pmarks_Ps.json: MT Ps.7.6 (=web 7.5) is the ONLY selah in Psalm 7, confirming the row's 'the psalm's one Selah occurrence' claim exactly, and it is used only as disclosed corroboration alongside the actual driver (the imperative shift opening the next strophe), not as the driver itself — policy-compliant. I independently tested a rival seam the row's rejected_alternative doesn't explicitly name: MT 7.2 and MT 7.4 (=web 7.1 and 7.3) open with the byte-identical vocative יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהַי ('Yahweh, my God'), which could be read as a renewed strophe-opening vocative separating the plea (7.1-2) from the oath (7.3-5). On inspection this does not outweigh the writer's grouping: the addressee and discourse register are unchanged across the repetition (no shift comparable to the addressee changes driving the Ps 5 and Ps 6 seams above), the lion-simile clause of v2 is syntactically a dependent פֶּן ('lest') purpose clause bound to v1's petition and cannot stand as a strophe end, and splitting at 7.2|7.3 would produce a two-verse orphan strophe below the book's norm without an independent addressee-level driver. The row's stated rejection ('no address shift') is terse but correct at its core; medium confidence appropriately reflects that this is a closer call than the Ps 5/6 seams. Not filed as a challenge — my own re-derivation confirms the row's conclusion holds.

ק֘וּמָ֤ה at web:Ps.7.6 (=oshb:Ps.7.7) collates at byte tier exactly as claimed. I tested the internal structure of this six-verse span for a rival split (e.g., between the imperative summons and the appeal for judgment) and found none of comparable strength: MT 7.7-12 (=web 7.6-11) forms one continuous appeal to Yahweh as judge with no addressee change and only one explicit vocative ('judge me, Yahweh' at v9=web8, matching the row's own citation) — the alternating imperative/jussive/declarative moods inside this span describe one sustained legal appeal, not competing movements. The seam against v12 rests on a genuine subject shift (from Yahweh/God as judge to third-person 'a man' who does not repent), a legitimate scene-shift driver. Medium confidence is appropriate given Psalm 7's three-part structure is more genuinely interpretive than the Ps 5/6 seams, but no better-warranted rival was found.

אִם לֹ֣א at web:Ps.7.12 (=oshb:Ps.7.13) and אוֹדֶ֣ה at web:Ps.7.17 (=oshb:Ps.7.18) both collate at byte tier exactly as claimed. The rejected_alternative (isolating v17 as its own row) is well-grounded beyond its stated reasoning: the book strategy's controlled vocabulary defines 'coda' narrowly as the five-book-boundary doxology/colophon closes (41:13, 72:18-20, 89:52, 106:48, arguably 150) — Ps 7:17 is not among them, so even under the rejected split there would be no correct controlled-vocabulary label for an isolated vow verse, reinforcing that grouping it with vv12-16 (rather than inventing an ill-fitting one-verse unit) was the sound choice. No addressee shift or vocative renewal separates v16 from v17 comparable to the drivers used elsewhere in this cluster. Confidence 'medium' is consistent with the other two Ps 7 strophe calls.

The refrain clause יְהוָ֤ה אֲדֹנֵ֗ינוּ מָֽה אַדִּ֣יר שִׁ֭מְךָ בְּכָל הָאָ֑רֶץ collates at exactly the tiers claimed: byte at web:Ps.8.1 (=oshb:Ps.8.2) and skeleton at web:Ps.8.9 (=oshb:Ps.8.10) — independently re-run via collate.py, confirming the row's own disclosed tier distinction (cantillation differs at the close, consonants recur) rather than overclaiming verbatim repetition. Title labels (mizmor, lamnatseach, le-David, al-haggittit) match the inventory exactly; shift+1 arithmetic (k=1) independently confirmed. unit_type=whole_psalm is the correct controlled-vocabulary choice, not refrain_unit: the refrain here functions as a bracketing inclusio around one continuous meditation (heavens, then human dominion), not as a lattice of repeated internal returns dividing the psalm into multiple strophes (contrast the refrain-lattice psalms named elsewhere in the campaign, e.g. 42-43, 46, 107). The book strategy's 'roughly <=8 vv' whole-psalm guideline is a soft norm ('roughly'), and Ps 8's 9 verses is a one-verse excess fully justified by the inclusio evidence itself, which is stronger than a bare length argument. The rejected_alternative (splitting into a frame row + body row) is correctly rejected: the frame verses are non-contiguous, so a 'frame row' would not be a coherent span. No selah in this span. Confidence 'high' matches the near-universal scholarly treatment of Psalm 8 as one indivisible hymn.
